# The PRCC rankings under the model's own viability constraint (#944)

*Generated by `scripts/prcc_under_admissibility.py`. Every figure is derived from the committed per-draw measurements; the generator hand-writes none.*

## The root artifact ranked the drivers of untreated death, and the row was read as sensitivity output

`analysis/prcc-results.json` defines the 11 swept rate constants and their ranges, and `uncertainty_intervals.py`, `sobol_sensitivity.py` and `headline_sensitivity.py` each load `metadata.parameter_ranges` from it so the analyses share one range source. `#936` measured that box as mostly inadmissible against the manuscript's untreated-viability constraint of 2% death under Control, and recorded that the published design could not have known because its conditions are treated arms only.

**The PRCC's conditions are not treated arms only.** `run_prcc.CONDITIONS` contains `Persister/Control`, and the committed artifact publishes its `mean_death_rate` as **14.6%** against that limit of 2% -- a factor of 7.3. The per-draw values were discarded, but a summary of the violation has been committed since the run, and every consumer reads only the ranges.

That row also names the mechanism. Its own `ranked_by_abs_prcc` opens `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate` -- the parameters `#936` and `#938` later measured as the ones the admissibility truncation selects on. The ordering was available in the root artifact before anything downstream measured it.

## Reproduction, which everything else rests on

The design is fully deterministic (draw `i` is evaluated at `seed = i + 100`, re-parsed from `run_prcc.py` rather than restated), so the published coefficients reproduce to float round-off rather than within a chosen tolerance. All 66 of them do: the largest deviation across every condition and parameter is 3.33e-16 against a bound of 1e-12. Reproduced, so the comparison below is with what is published.

## How much of the design is admissible, and how precisely that can be said

Judged on the same 3 untreated arms and the same imported constraint the sibling pages use (`Glycolytic/Control`, `Persister/Control`, `PersisterNrf2/Control`): **841 of 2000 draws (42.0%)** satisfy it. Median worst untreated death 3.4%, worst 92.0%.

**That fraction is resolution-limited, and this family of pages quotes one to a decimal place.** The constraint is a threshold on a Monte-Carlo estimate and the boundary cuts through the dense part of the worst-untreated distribution, so a draw near it lands on either side depending on the per-draw seed. The same draws, re-judged:

| cells per arm | admissible counts across seeds | mean | range |
|--:|---|--:|---|
| 1000 | 785, 909, 843 | 42.28% | 39.2%-45.5% (124 draws) |
| 2000 | 774, 883, 850 | 41.78% | 38.7%-44.1% (109 draws) |
| 8000 | 770, 803, 781 | 39.23% | 38.5%-40.2% (33 draws) |

So the admissible fraction of one box over one set of draws moves by 124 draws on the seed alone at the lowest resolution here. **AND IT FALLS WITH RESOLUTION**, 42.28% at 1000 cells per arm against 39.23% at 8000, while the seed spread collapses from 124 draws to 33. Monotone across every count measured. A fraction judged at the lower counts therefore reads HIGH, which is the direction that makes `#936`'s conclusion stronger rather than weaker -- and it is the opposite of the direction predicted before measuring, on the argument that a maximum over noisy arms overestimates the maximum and so should bias the admissible fraction down. That argument is refuted here and is recorded rather than removed.

Nothing substantive turns on it: *most of the prior is inadmissible* survives a band this wide comfortably. What does not survive is quoting the fraction to a decimal place as a property of the box, and `#938`'s cross-page agreement statistic compares two such fractions through a binomial standard error, which models the sampling of draws and not the classification of one. The agreement it reports is unaffected -- a wider band makes two fractions agree more easily, not less.

## The rankings, conditioned

| condition | mean (full -> admissible) | std | top three (full) | top three (admissible) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Persister/SDT` | 0.998004 -> 0.995926 | 0.009579 -> 0.014321 | `sdt_ros`, `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_propagation` | `sdt_ros`, `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_rate` |
| `Persister/RSL3` | 0.521712 -> 0.280213 | 0.327287 -> 0.262905 | `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate`, `lp_rate` | `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate`, `lp_rate` |
| `Glycolytic/SDT` | 0.816122 -> 0.707195 | 0.294615 -> 0.353114 | `sdt_ros`, `lp_rate`, `lp_propagation` | `sdt_ros`, `lp_rate`, `fsp1_rate` |
| `Glycolytic/RSL3` | 0.000002 -> 0.000000 | 0.000055 -> 0.000000 | `gpx4_rate`, `lp_rate`, `fsp1_rate` | **undefined** (constant output) |
| `Persister/Control` *(the arm conditioned on)* | 0.146437 -> 0.004564 | 0.211182 -> 0.005248 | `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate` | `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate` |
| `PersisterNrf2/SDT` | 0.948489 -> 0.897781 | 0.144479 -> 0.204212 | `sdt_ros`, `gsh_scav_efficiency`, `lp_rate` | `sdt_ros`, `lp_rate`, `gsh_scav_efficiency` |

**`Glycolytic/RSL3` has no conditioned ranking at all.** Its output is constant across the admissible subset, so a rank partial correlation is undefined and none is published here. On the full design the condition contains 4 dead cells across 2,000,000 simulated, so its published ranking is an ordering of correlations against that many events; conditioning removes them.

**One mechanism, opposite effects on attribution.** Admissibility keeps the draws whose defences are strong enough that an untreated cell survives, which DE-SATURATES the exogenous-ROS arms -- the output standard deviation rises on 3 of 3 of them, giving the defence parameters variance to be attributed -- while pushing the inducer arm toward its floor. It is the same two-directional structure `#936` found in the intervals, showing up in the rankings.

The arm being conditioned on is reported as a diagnostic and not as a result: selecting draws on an outcome and then reporting that outcome's sensitivity is selection on the dependent variable.

## What Chapter 5 quotes, scored

Both figures are parsed from `article/drafts/v1.md`, not typed here.

> For Persister × SDT, a single parameter dominates: sdt_ros (+0.63, exogenous ROS dose); all other parameters have |PRCC| < 0.16

`sdt_ros` stays dominant and strengthens, +0.6295 -> +0.7302 (still the top-ranked parameter). **The quoted bound of 0.16 does not survive**: 0 parameters reach it on the full design and 3 do on the admissible subset -- `gsh_scav_efficiency` at 0.1976, `lp_rate` at 0.1855, `lp_propagation` at 0.1671. So the asymmetry the sentence describes survives conditioning and the number it puts on the other parameters does not.

> For Persister × RSL3, the LP cascade parameters dominate: lp_propagation (PRCC = +0.92), gpx4_rate (−0.87), and lp_rate (+0.80) — the death outcome is a balance between LP accumulation and enzymatic repair, with five parameters showing |PRCC| > 0.4

The 3 named parameters `lp_propagation`, `gpx4_rate`, `lp_rate` remain the top three in the same order. **The quoted count does not survive**: parameters above 0.4 go 5 on the full design (reproducing the sentence) to 4 on the admissible subset.

Neither sentence is edited. Each is true of the prior it cites, and the deliverable here is that the two bounds are measured under the restriction rather than assumed to carry over. The rankings -- what the sentences are for -- hold.

## Is the comparison circular?

If conditioning selected on the DRUG parameters, a change in an SDT ranking would be partly an artifact of keeping weaker-drug draws. Each parameter's admissible mean against its full-prior mean, as a fraction of its own range (strong selection at 0.1):

| parameter | full | admissible | shift | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| `gsh_scav_efficiency` | 0.500 | 0.320 | -0.180 | **strongly selected** |
| `lp_propagation` | 0.500 | 0.384 | -0.116 | **strongly selected** |
| `gpx4_rate` | 0.500 | 0.603 | +0.103 | **strongly selected** |
| `lp_rate` | 0.500 | 0.414 | -0.086 |  |
| `nrf2_gsh_rate` | 0.500 | 0.572 | +0.072 |  |
| `death_threshold` | 0.500 | 0.527 | +0.027 |  |
| `fenton_rate` | 0.500 | 0.476 | -0.024 |  |
| `fsp1_rate` | 0.500 | 0.523 | +0.023 |  |
| `gpx4_degradation_by_ros` | 0.500 | 0.505 | +0.005 |  |
| `rsl3_gpx4_inhib` | 0.500 | 0.495 | -0.005 | drug |
| `sdt_ros` | 0.500 | 0.502 | +0.002 | drug |

**Clear.** The largest drug-parameter shift is 0.005 against a bar of 0.1, so the rankings move because the defences kept are stronger and not because the drug kept is weaker. That matters more here than on the sibling pages, because the claim under test is about a drug parameter's dominance.

## The admissible subset is not a Latin hypercube

LHS buys one draw per stratum per margin, so on the full design every margin sits within a draw-width of uniform -- 61 times tighter than a random sample of the same size would give, which is what the design is for. A filtered subset is SMALLER, though, and a smaller sample deviates more whatever was filtered, so each margin is reported against the deviation a random subsample of the admissible size would show (0.0469 at the 5% level):

| parameter | full | admissible | times the same-size null |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `gsh_scav_efficiency` | 0.0005 | 0.2913 | 6.21 |
| `lp_propagation` | 0.0005 | 0.1811 | 3.86 |
| `gpx4_rate` | 0.0005 | 0.1641 | 3.50 |
| `lp_rate` | 0.0005 | 0.1332 | 2.84 |
| `nrf2_gsh_rate` | 0.0005 | 0.1165 | 2.48 |
| `death_threshold` | 0.0005 | 0.0485 | 1.03 |
| `fenton_rate` | 0.0005 | 0.0419 | 0.89 |
| `fsp1_rate` | 0.0005 | 0.0399 | 0.85 |
| `gpx4_degradation_by_ros` | 0.0005 | 0.0220 | 0.47 |
| `sdt_ros` | 0.0005 | 0.0169 | 0.36 |
| `rsl3_gpx4_inhib` | 0.0005 | 0.0160 | 0.34 |

The loss is UNEVEN and it lands exactly where the selection table says it should: `gsh_scav_efficiency` deviates by 0.2913, 6.2 times the same-size null, against `rsl3_gpx4_inhib` at 0.0160 or 0.3 times it -- so the least-deformed margins are within what having fewer draws explains and the selected ones are not. So the conditioned coefficients are rank partial correlations over a filtered sample, not over an LHS design: a comparison between two populations rather than between two designs, and the stratification LHS exists to provide is gone from 6 of 11 margins.

## The escalation decision in the same artifact

`sobol_decision` publishes `warranted: false` on 2 flags against a threshold of more than two, i.e. one flag from flipping, and the manuscript repeats the call. Recomputed on the PRCC's own conditions it reproduces (2 flags) and **survives conditioning**: 2 flags on the admissible subset, `warranted: false`. The divergences themselves move AWAY from the threshold.

| half | flags | warranted |
|---|---|---|
| published | 2 (`sdt_ros` in `Persister/SDT` (0.296), `sdt_ros` in `PersisterNrf2/SDT` (0.336)) | False |
| full | 2 (`sdt_ros` in `Persister/SDT` (0.296), `sdt_ros` in `PersisterNrf2/SDT` (0.336)) | False |
| admissible | 2 (`sdt_ros` in `Persister/SDT` (0.291), `sdt_ros` in `PersisterNrf2/SDT` (0.265)) | False |

A first pass recomputed this over the untreated arms as well and got one flag more than the artifact publishes, which would have been a reproduction failure reported as a conditioning effect. The recomputation is restricted to the published condition set, and the reproduction is asserted before the conditioned half is read.

## The Sobol design cannot be conditioned, only characterised

`sobol_sensitivity.py` screens the same ranges over 10 of these parameters (excluding `sdt_ros`) with a Saltelli base of 2048. Its A and B samples are 40.7% and 39.6% admissible -- but the estimator does not consume rows, it consumes PAIRS: Jansen's total effect differences each A row against the same row with one column swapped in from B. So the question is how many of those pairs STRADDLE the constraint, one side a cell the model says is already dead untreated and the other not.

| parameter | admissible after swap | straddling pairs |
|---|--:|--:|
| `gsh_scav_efficiency` | 40.9% | 633 (30.9%) |
| `lp_propagation` | 38.5% | 382 (18.7%) |
| `gpx4_rate` | 39.6% | 328 (16.0%) |
| `lp_rate` | 41.0% | 272 (13.3%) |
| `nrf2_gsh_rate` | 40.3% | 253 (12.4%) |
| `fenton_rate` | 40.2% | 83 (4.1%) |
| `death_threshold` | 40.9% | 60 (2.9%) |
| `fsp1_rate` | 40.6% | 39 (1.9%) |
| `gpx4_degradation_by_ros` | 40.7% | 0 (0.0%) |
| `rsl3_gpx4_inhib` | 40.7% | 0 (0.0%) |

**This is why filtering is not available as a correction.** The straddling fraction runs from 0.0% to 30.9%: dropping straddling pairs would strip `gsh_scav_efficiency` of 30.9% of its pairs and `gpx4_degradation_by_ros`, `rsl3_gpx4_inhib` of none, so the filtered estimator would compare a parameter stripped of its largest moves against one left intact. Re-running Saltelli inside the admissible region is not available either: admissibility is a constraint surface rather than a box, and rejection sampling breaks the column independence between A and B that the estimator assumes. The design can be characterised and not conditioned.

The parameters whose cross-swaps straddle most are the ones the published decomposition attributes most to, which is not a coincidence: moving a defence parameter far enough to change the kill rate is the same move that kills the untreated cell. `gsh_scav_efficiency` is the sharpest case -- the report flags it NOT identifiable from the kill rate, and it is both the highest-straddling parameter here and the one the PRCC's own Control row ranks first as a driver of untreated death. The verdict survives conditioning (its coefficient on the inducer arm falls rather than rises), so what is withdrawn is not the verdict but the reading that the parameter does not matter: its influence lands on untreated viability rather than on treatment response, which the kill observable cannot see.

The excluded parameter is evaluated at its default in the untreated arms above, which is only sound if it is inert there. Measured rather than assumed: across every untreated arm, the death rate at the bottom and the top of its range is bit-identical.

## What this does not establish

- **Conditioning is not inference.** It removes draws and adds no data, so `identifiability-report.json`'s data-conditioned-headline count stays where it is, and a guard breaks if that report ever says otherwise.
- **No ranking here is a calibration.** Both halves are sensitivity over an uncalibrated box; the restriction changes which draws the box contains, not whether any parameter is anchored to data.
- **The admissible half is not a design.** See the stratification table: it is a filtered sample, and no property LHS guarantees can be claimed for it.
- **The fraction is not comparable to the sibling pages' by subtraction.** Those sample uniformly where this is a Latin hypercube, at a different per-draw seed convention, so the difference is a design difference and not a disagreement about the box.
- **Admissibility is judged on 3 phenotypes, the same ones the sibling pages use**, so the fraction is an upper bound in the same way theirs is.
